differences.what: A fixes the network's constants: h=100, v=C(100,3)=161700, N=v^3, m=h^3=10^6 (S1.3.0) and I=3v^2=78440670000 invocations with wire counts W_b=2N+I(v z_b+c_b), W_c (S1.3.3); B states none of these numbers.

A states the neighbour rules (bit: |S cap T|=1; complex: distinct triples with even intersection) and the complex side-injection coefficient -(|S cap T|-1)/2; B states the cancellations without saying which pairs are neighbours.

items.note: Both plans carry all four checklist sub-steps (B1 to B4: scratch-independent net change, bit and complex coefficients, three-stage signed swap). A also gives the network's constants and neighbour rules, which B leaves out. This is a minor completeness difference.

Both state the invariant, that the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the per-route operator with sign (A S1.4.1-S1.4.3, B S5.3.1-S5.3.3), checked against lines 804-825. No difference of substance.

differences.what: The per-edge residual table (residual and dimension for every data, center, side and scratch edge) is given in full by A; B only says that every edge joins comparable labels and that the non-central edges are nondecreasing.

For the side edge 2->5, A gives the residual P (x) <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2, which exists because t_X is orthogonal to t_Y. B states only the inclusion <t_X> in t_Y^perp, without the complement or its dimension h-2.
Over F_2 every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating and so has an orthonormal basis. A states this; B never justifies that the orthonormal bases exist.
A gives the stage label transitions and shows that they match the next stage's labels and the terminals; B lacks this.

items.note: Both carry L3 (only the center 3->4 edges decrease, telescoping to Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich) and L5 (100/539, 101/539). A also carries L1, L2 and L4, which B lacks: B has no residual table, only the inclusion half of L2, and nothing on orthonormal bases.

differences.what: A derives the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m from P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}; B uses the condition only as a premise in the power-width step.
B gives the reason the rank equals the dimension change: P_V-P_U is the identity on V cap U^perp and zero on its complement, and reversing an edge negates it. A states the rank only.

items.note: Both have s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m with the N extra ranks from the 2P_{U_a} source edges. Each plan has one small justification the other lacks, and the two differences balance.

differences.what: A treats the multi-column case: the telescoped phase frames give C^{(x) mk} on every role over k columns. B never mentions columns.
A writes the phase frame explicitly as C_U = H^{(x)m} diag(i^{q_U(x)}) H^{(x)m}; B only says that the frames are defined from Hamming weight mod 4.

items.note: P1 (weight additivity mod 4 over an orthonormal residual basis) and P2 (odd weight gives the translation kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse) are present in both. P4 is partial in both: A cites the zero and full label frames and undoes the signed exchange, while B states that the exceptional pair carries C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates. Only A covers the k-column tensoring (P3, partly) and gives the explicit frame.

Both plans carry R1 to R4: L<N/2 so the deficits are positive, eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500, both above 20*2^-50, log m<20 so s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^-50 (A S1.5.6-S1.5.10.3, B S5.4.6, S5.4.7.3, S5.6-S5.6.3). Checked at lines 1105-1110 and 1319-1343.

differences.what: A gives the derivations behind the linear-time primitives: q^2-stream split for digit permutations, the row split r=Wg+w, the cyclic shift done by splitting each fiber at Q-a and merging in reverse, absorption of offset work via b^C=O(q^b), and multiplication by c through c increasing pieces. B states the two lemmas only.

items.note: Both state the O(V) elementary operations and the controlled shifts with b^{O(1)} offsets. Only A gives how they are derived, which matters little for this supporting item.

differences.what: A gives the elimination proof of A=E_1 Pi E_2: pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing by lower-triangular operations, repeating on the active indices, Pi with exactly a ones, E_1=L^{-1}, E_2=R^{-1}. B only states the factorization.
A chooses a fixed odd prime that avoids every denominator and diagonal numerator in the finite factor table, so the factors stay invertible mod q^b. B only asserts that a fixed odd prime exists.

items.note: M3 (O(V) lower-triangular transforms in descending order) and M4 (one interchange per one of Pi, a in all) are present in both. A also carries M1 and M2, and B lacks both.

Both carry the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, the edge shears Phi_{A_e} by rank-many recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every role, the three-update interchange, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved by the geometric sum with both cases, the O(V) depth-first schedule and descriptor absorption (A S1.8.1-S1.8.7.2, B S5.9.1-S5.9.8; lines 1491-1615). Small extra details on each side balance.

differences.what: A covers widths that differ by one bit, using one extra single-bit move with the equal-width interchange. B lacks this case.

items.note: Both give the high-digit row field R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, the padding to R'<2R, the base-m decomposition with O(V)sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau) and the binary padding to [q^e]. Only A adds the unequal-width case that the paper treats.

differences.what: A gives the reason for the coordinate form, P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}, and the identities C^2=X, C^4=I, C^{-1}=bI+aX=-iZCZ. B states the coordinate form without the conjugation identity.

B gives the Gaussian elimination of M into at most m(m-1)+3m elementary row additions, each XORing corresponding selected bits of two whole slots. A says only that the change of basis is a fixed number of row additions.

items.note: Both have the inverse-child identity, exactly s_c child calls on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D. Each plan has one small step the other lacks, so the item is a tie.

Both carry the eight parity operations and their composed permutation, guard values in [10,2^{K-1}-11] with no carry under displacement eight, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^-K} by the union bound, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting only B, sixteen swaps and eight rotations, radix-sort repair, the cost terms and the change-of-basis cost O(V((eK)^tau+1)) (A S2.2.1-S2.2.10, B S5.11.5.1-S5.11.5.9; lines 2013-2231).

differences.what: A gives the row-axis constants q_0=ceil(log_2 W)ceil(log_m(2d)) and k_0=ceil(log_m d); B uses q_0 without defining it.
B notes that the leaf bound also covers a<1 by taking sigma>=0, and that each edge call's volume is exactly 1/W of its parent's.

items.note: Both carry the recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), leaves O(e) below d^beta, overhead O(e^lambda), the geometric internal sum, the leaf bound e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)} and the base-m pieces giving O(d^lambda'). The remaining differences are minor and point both ways.

differences.what: A gives the values nu=11, C_1=20 for the stated network and the explicit per-invocation bound 24W^3+4s+4W+4<E. B gives the definitions of nu and C_1 but not their values.
B notes that the depth recurrence concatenates the s calls and so uses s, not s/W, and checks that the packed-call cost terms vanish uniformly over all allowed d,r.

items.note: All five checklist sub-steps S1 to S5 are present in both: the constants E, B, nu, C_1, C_0, Delta; A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with leaf 8e; unrolling to C_0 d^{C_1}; exact representation with p+Delta and Delta+3 bits and Delta=o(p); and absolute row sum one with error below sqrt2 2^-p. The extra details on each side are small and balance.

Both carry character cancellation by the pairing shift, contraction, decimation in frequency with bit-reversed storage, H_0^2=I/2 for the opposite procedure, the grouped round with a recordwise monomial, the layout L, the three cost terms, the error sqrt2*l*2^-p and the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1} (A S3.1-S3.3.6, B S6.1-S6.3.7). Minor extras on each side balance.

Both evaluate at B_0=2^{4p}, form four products with the established multiplier, use the bound |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, recover by centred residues, apply the negacyclic reduction and give the O(rp log(rp)) cost (A S3.4.1-S3.4.6, B S6.4.1-S6.4.5; lines 3233-3368).

Both carry the convolution identity with the scale M, the permutation LB commuting with the pointwise product (B as a step, A in its method and motivation), the error chain 2delta, then 3delta+eta, then M(3delta+eta), and the cost (A S3.5.1-S3.5.6, B S6.5-S6.7; lines 3414-3495).

Both carry the Gaussian identity, the Neumann inversion of N=CTD, the contractions A=S', B_0=D'J'C with normalisation 2^{-2alpha^2}, the map errors and costs, tensoring to RF_s=2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A, the line costs and axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)) (A S4.1.1-S4.1.9, B S7.1.1-S7.1.10).

Both carry the chirp period, the coefficient computation giving QF_t, F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+ leading to RF_s^+R=F_s^+, the cancellation to (u*v)/S^2 and the conjugation remark (A S4.2.1-S4.2.6, B S7.2.1-S7.2.5; lines 3938-3988).

differences.what: A states the fixed rational exponents tau=sigma=1-2^-50, beta=1/2, delta=1/16, lambda=1-2^-52, c=2^-56, lambda'=1-2^-54. B's parameter step lists only C_1, epsilon and kappa, and B never gives lambda, c, lambda' or delta.
A verifies the layer conditions: tau(1+c/beta)<1-31*2^-55<lambda and sigma+beta(1-sigma)=1-2^-51<lambda<lambda'<1. B lacks this check.

items.note: Both carry the sizes b, p, d, K, T, r, the axis lengths, the comparison constants, alpha and gamma, the prime-interval count, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the n^{o(1)} search and the no-wraparound bound. Only A gives most of the fixed exponents and the check that they satisfy the layer conditions.

Both carry the CRT isomorphism with mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i, the triangular formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i}a_jP_j, updates in order i=d..1 as rotations of the valid interval keeping padding zero, and the O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)) cost with O(d^2) axis moves (A S5.2.1-S5.2.6, B S8.2.1-S8.2.5; lines 4204-4296).

Both carry the well-definedness (zeta y)^r=1, the diagonal isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, and the computed twist with errors below 4 each (A S5.3.1-S5.3.2 and S5.9.1.2, B S8.3.1-S8.3.4 and S8.5.9.3).

Both carry the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A=RF_s, its conjugate opposite, digits as numerators a_j 2^{p-b-2}, and the six algorithm steps with the two S scalings explained by (u*v)/S^2 (A S5 method, S5.3.3-S5.8 and S5.9.2.1; B S8.4.1-S8.5.8; lines 4415-4544). Small extras on each side, such as B's chirp numerator mod 2r and A's digit reading, balance.

differences.what: A gives the carry recurrence k_0=0, d_j=(c_j+k_j) mod 2^b, k_{j+1}=floor((c_j+k_j)/2^b), and shows that exactly 2n bits are output because the product is below 2^{2n}. B gives only the carry bound and invariant, and lists the 2n-bit output as an algorithm step.

items.note: Both carry the full error chain: E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, then (2E_s+2) and (3E_s+2), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, the final error 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, and exact rounding. A adds a little more on the carry stage.

differences.what: A gives each table row's power of p and all seven margin formulas g_1..g_7 (for example g_4=1-tau-epsilon(2-tau), g_5=1/4-delta-3epsilon/2) before substituting. B lists the normalised costs without their powers (except the Gaussian row) and gives only the margin values, with g_2=epsilon c(1-tau) as the one formula.

items.note: Both reach min g_i=g_2=2^-181=2kappa, show that the powers are at most 1-2kappa with log factors at most p^kappa, account for setup and exceptional sorting, and give O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}). A gives the margins in full.

differences.what: A's root claim states that the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. B never states the disproof. Neither plan gives the liminf argument.

items.note: Only A states the conclusion this supporting item supports, and it does not give the reasoning. B has nothing on this item.

chain.note: Both trees reach the theorem by the paper's route: the bank-exchange network with frames and labels, s<Wm, tau=sigma=1-2^-50, then the power-width and arbitrary-width interchange and the layer recurrence, synthetic transforms and convolution, resampling and chirp, and finally recovery and cost. Their dependencies match the paper. B thins out at two core links of the central saving: it gives no residual table, no h-2 side residual and no reason the orthonormal bases exist behind L=Ich and s_c, and no factorization proof or prime choice behind 'calls = rank'. It also gives the final margins without their formulas. A carries all of these.

overall.reason: I found no misstatement of the paper in either plan, so the decision rests on completeness. On the central saving, A carries the label-residual sub-steps L1, L2 and L4 and the matrix-shear sub-steps M1 and M2, which B lacks, so B's chain to s<Wm and 'calls = rank' is thinner. A is also more complete on the fixed parameters and their layer-condition check, the margin formulas, the network constants and the multi-column phase case. B has nothing of substance that A lacks beyond small details that balance out (rank reason, Gaussian-elimination count, depth-uses-s remark).
